newsitem.title: USA: Pen Interconnect sets labor cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: Pen Interconnect sets labor cost cuts.

text.p: Pen Interconnect Inc said Tuesday it is completing moves to reduce labor costs by 15 percent and will continue to implement companywide policies to lower operating expenses and improve manufacturing margins.
The efforts are expected to have immediate positive effects on operations and will play a major role in establishing new levels of profitability in fiscal 1997, ending September 30.
There have been labor force reductions at Pen's Salt Lake City; Tustin, Calif.; and San Jose, Calif., plants which were accomplished through layoffs, the company said.

In addition, the company announced the appointment of Mohrdad Mobasseri as the new general manager for Pen's Tustin-based InCirT Division, its profitable and expanding EMSI contract manufacturing operations. Mobasseri assumes his post immediately at the Tustin facility.

It also said that Carl Rasmussen, formerly general manager of the Salt Lake City operations, will concentrate on major accounts and developing manufacturing opportunities with companies needing total turnkey contract manufacturing.
Pen said it also plans to improve the efficiency of its high-volume manufacturing operations in mainland China.
The new China policies include the appointment of Dale Acord as the company's first quality and production engineering liaison, effective immediately.
